newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 20.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* SBC Communications Inc said it expects to post one-time charges in the 1997 fiscal year of up to $2.3 billion in connection with its merger with Pacific Telesis Group PAC.N.
* Tobacco negotiators are hopeful of reaching a settlement as early as Friday.
* The U.S. trade deficit grew 7.8 percent in April, drawing new attention to tensions with Japan and China as world leaders gather in Denver for a summit meeting.

* A British judge has ruled that two penniless activists libeled McDonald's Corp when it said the fast-food giant had destroyed rain forests, discriminated against employees and poisoned its customers.

* News Corp Ltd and Tele-Communications Inc are close to a deal to buy 40 percent of Cablevision Systems Corp's sports-programming assets, including Madison Square Garden properties, for $850 million.
* Intel Corp Chief Executive Andy Grove has a vision for the future, and it is this: the personal computer is about to surpass the video-game machine as the vehicle of choice to play computer games.
* Unisys Corp Chairman and Chief Executive James Unruh said he will resign, but will help to find a successor.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 58.35 points, closing at 7777.06, just five points off the record high.
* A federal judge has ruled that International Paper Co cannot enforce a noncompete pact against an executive who left and went to become chairman and chief executive of Louisiana-Pacific Corp.
* The New York Cotton Exchange and the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange are considering a possible merger.
* Merrill Lynch and Co Inc has agreed to pay $30 million to settle a criminal investigation into the firm's role in the 1994 collapse of Orange County, Calif.'s investment pool.
* Big Board short interest rose 4.8 percent to a record 3.44 billion shares.
* Nissan Motor Co Ltd is lowering the suggested retail price on its 1998 Nissan Altima by 8 percent.
* Chicago's grain traders are eyeing predictions that a strong El Nino weather pattern will boost crops in the Midwest and poor growing conditions in major farm areas of Australia and China.
* Advertising prices are rising in the radio industry as the bevy of acquisitions that occurred in the past year has put stations into fewer hands.
* Heard on the Street: Major oil companies have been able to weather a drop in oil prices by trimming excess costs and choosing their projects carefully -- all leading to rising stock prices.

* Credit Markets: Investors are willing to take chances on bonds from emerging markets as evidenced by Thursday's Russian Federation sale of $2 billion of high-yield bonds, the largest deal ever in the Euro/144a sector.
